assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines magic-wavelength trapping with narrow clock transitions and has pushed frequency measurement to the 1e-18 level. It exemplifies the principle that progress rests on what we can measure and how accurately. It underpins redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea is original and clean, and the impact is already broad.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and led its first realizations with strontium. Ye's group drove the record-accuracy clocks and the many-body and systematic-control advances. A two-person prize is natural. Earlier recognition of Hall and Haensch for combs and laser spectroscopy is separate and does not crowd this out.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmations in several laboratories and species, with agreement at the 1e-18 level and international clock comparisons. The interpretation is stable. Redefinition of the second is still pending, but the physics is mature, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether other contributors, such as ion-clock developers, would be argued to share credit.
Overlap with prior frequency-metrology prizes could be raised against it.
Redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled trapped ions and neutral atoms as platforms for quantum computation and simulation. This has defined the quantum-information agenda in atomic physics. The ion-trap proposal, experimental gates and entanglement of many ions, and the simulation paradigm together constitute a major, lasting body of work.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive 1995 ion-trap proposal and the later simulation and cold-atom theory. Blatt led the experimental realization of gates, entanglement and digital simulation. Bloch is credited in the candidate but is better associated with the separate lattice-simulation entry, so a Cirac, Zoller, Blatt trio is cleaner. Other trapped-ion groups, such as Wineland's, were recognized in 2012.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups, and now commercially active. The platform is well established, although the long-term computational advantage is not demonstrated. It is mature as physics, but overlap with the 2012 prize and with the Bloch lattice entry needs sorting out.
uncertainties: The scope is compound, mixing a theory proposal, ion experiments and cold-atom simulation, which could blur the citation.
Overlap with the 2012 Wineland and Haroche prize.
Unclear whether Bloch should be included instead of Blatt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and is the architecture behind most superconducting quantum processors. Conceptually it is a quantum-optics idea realized in a new medium, with large impact on readout, control and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Blais made the theoretical proposal with collaborators, Wallraff the first strong-coupling demonstration with Schoelkopf's group, and Schoelkopf the broader development including transmon-based coherence. Credit looks assignable to these three, though Yale colleagues such as Girvin and Devoret are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and technologically relevant. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits, which is a related area, so a second circuits prize so soon may be viewed as premature.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 superconducting circuit prize.
Girvin, Devoret and others are part of the story but are not credited names in this entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms is both a deep demonstration of quantum mechanics and a basis for precision sensing of gravity, rotation and constants. It has direct links to the measurement-accuracy theme and to cold-atom control.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard and Mlynek demonstrated the first atom interferometers in 1991, Kasevich built the high-precision light-pulse sensors. Chu, who is intertwined with the light-pulse method, is not among the credited names, and so the configuration is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: The physics is established, and applications in gravimetry and inertial navigation have matured. Long-baseline tests are still developing, so the main impact is solid but partly still ahead.
uncertainties: Chu, Bordé and others are not in the credited list, which complicates attribution.
Prior prizes for laser cooling may be regarded as covering part of the ground.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with the HgTe experimental observation, opened a field of topological materials with far-reaching conceptual impact beyond the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theory. Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Zhang and Hughes are not credited names, so credit is incomplete. The experimental half is also split between several 3D materials groups.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials and used in spintronics and quantum-computing proposals. The impact is mature although practical applications are still limited.
uncertainties: Key contributors to the HgTe proposal and 3D topological insulators are absent from the credited names.
Relation to the 2016 Nobel prize needs to be judged.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade produces strong, controllable interactions between neutral atoms, and programmable tweezer arrays now reach hundreds of qubits for simulation and computation. It is an important and fast-moving platform, in my own area of quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: Lukin's group has driven many-body quantum simulation and the coherent control of large arrays, Browaeys the first experimental blockade and entanglement in single atoms, Saffman the gate proposals. The original blockade proposal credits Jaksch, Cirac, Zoller and Lukin, so attribution is contested.
assessment.maturity: Rapid progress but still evolving. Interpretation of quantum-advantage claims is not yet stable. Probably premature compared with more settled entries.
uncertainties: Original blockade proposal credit is split and some proposers are not credited here.
Impact on actual computation is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a room-temperature quantum sensor for magnetic and electric fields, temperature and nanoscale imaging. This directly serves the idea of measuring more precisely and has many applications in biology and materials.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first detected and manipulated single NV spins. Lukin contributed sensing and quantum register concepts. Other groups, such as Awschalom, Hanson and Yacoby, made comparably important contributions, which weakens the proposed configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed widely and applied in diverse fields. The sensing field is still maturing, and no single decisive claim of practical dominance exists.
uncertainties: Several major contributors are not in the credited list.
Whether the discovery is the physics of single-spin detection or the sensor application is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical coherence tomography is a major biomedical optical imaging technique, based on low-coherence interferometry, with large clinical impact especially in ophthalmology. I am familiar with optical imaging in scattering tissue and see it as a significant instrumentation advance, though the question is whether it is physics.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Science paper by Huang, Swanson, Fujimoto and collaborators established OCT. Earlier low-coherence work by Fercher and others complicates priority, and the Science authorship list is large.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for three decades. Timing is not an issue, but the physics prize fit may be debated against a medicine or engineering award.
uncertainties: Priority questions with earlier low-coherence interferometry work.
Fit to the physics prize remit is uncertain.
